transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. It's really nice to meet you. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Well, um... it's probably nothing too serious, I don't want to make a huge fuss out of it, but I just haven't been feeling quite right lately. What really made me come in is that the things that usually make me feel like, you know, myself... they've just started feeling a little flat. Or heavy, I guess? 

Like, I usually love going on these long photography walks, and I do some mentoring with the kids in my neighborhood. Even just my day-to-day routine—I'm an executive assistant, so keeping a perfectly clean, color-coded calendar is usually my pride and joy. But lately, I just... I don't know, I just stopped initiating any of it. I'm still getting by, of course, I don't want to sound like I'm complaining. It's just taking a lot more effort to care about those things. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that right, I just thought it might be best to get it checked out.
How long have you been feeling this way—has it been a couple of weeks, a few months, or longer?

Well, um... I guess it's been a little longer than a few months. Probably about, oh, a year and three months? Give or take. 

It kind of started around the time my... well, a family member of mine, their health started declining and their behavior changed a bit. I had to step in and take on a lot more of the coordination for their care and everything. Which is fine! I mean, it's what you do for family, right? I'm happy to help them. 

But I think maybe just the extra responsibility sort of... I don't know, maybe it just caught up with me a little bit? Is it normal to feel a bit drained after taking on something like that? I just really want to make sure I'm not overreacting.

Over this past year and three months, have you been feeling this way pretty much every day without much let-up, or have there been stretches of time—days or weeks—where you felt more like your usual self?

Well, um... I wouldn't say it's been every single day without any let-up. I mean, I definitely have good days! I try really hard to focus on the positive, you know? 

There are definitely times where I feel a bit more like myself, where I can get through the day without it feeling like such a chore. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around moping all the time. I still go to work, I still try to keep a smile on my face for the kids I mentor. 

But I guess... if I'm being completely honest, the stretches where I feel totally normal are probably shorter than the times where I feel, um, a bit heavy. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. I'm trying my best to push through it, I really am.
Besides feeling flat or heavy, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels, or trouble concentrating, during this time?

Well, um, my appetite and concentration are mostly fine, I think. I really try to stay on top of things. But my sleep... I guess my sleep has been a little different lately? It's actually been kind of helpful, though, so I don't want to make it sound like a bad thing! 

There have been some nights where I'll only sleep for maybe, oh, two or three hours, and I'll wake up way before dawn. But instead of feeling exhausted or dragging my feet, I actually feel completely ready to go. I'll just hop right up and start answering emails or updating my boss's appointment lists. It's actually really nice to get a head start on the day before everyone else is awake, honestly. 

I know all the health articles say you need eight hours, so I hope I'm not doing any harm by just rolling with it when I have that extra energy. I just figure, why fight it if I'm getting things done, right? Does that sound okay to you, or is that something I should be trying to fix?

When you have those nights of little sleep and feel full of energy, does that heightened, 'ready-to-go' feeling typically last for several days in a row—along with things like talking faster, feeling unusually confident, or taking on more projects than usual—or is it usually just that one night?

Well, um... yeah, it does usually stick around for a few days at a time. I wouldn't say I get unusually confident or anything like that, I just... I just feel really productive. 

During those stretches, I'll start rebuilding work templates, making detailed care plans for my family member, emailing relatives to keep them in the loop, and reorganizing all my files at once. It just feels like... like if I sit still, I'm dropping the ball, you know? There's just so much to do, and I really want to make sure I'm doing a good job and taking care of everyone. 

I hope it doesn't sound like I'm taking on too much. I just want to be helpful. Is it okay that I get so much done during those times, or do you think I should be trying to pace myself more?

During those few days when you're feeling extra energetic and getting so much done, have other people—like coworkers, family, or friends—commented that you seem different than usual, such as more talkative, easily distracted, or unusually keyed up?

Well, um... I guess people have mentioned it a little bit. I don't want to make it sound like I'm being disruptive or anything! I just get so excited about getting things organized for everyone. 

But, um, my wife and some of my coworkers... they have said that I talk a bit faster than normal when I'm like that. They say I'll jump from talking about filling out medical forms for my family member, to hitting my work deadlines, to, you know, ideas for the kids I mentor... and I guess I do it so quickly that they have a hard time getting a word in edgewise. 

I just have so many thoughts going at once and I really want to share them and get everything sorted out. I try to be mindful of it, I really do. I hope I'm not annoying them when I get like that. Do you think that's something I need to work on being more polite about? I just want to make sure I'm communicating well.

During those few days of high energy and rapid talking, did it ever cause serious problems—like conflicts at work, risky decisions, or needing someone to step in—or were you still able to function normally despite people noticing the change?

Oh, no, no serious conflicts or risky decisions at all! I really pride myself on keeping things running smoothly for everyone, you know? I'd say my work has stayed intact overall. I definitely haven't needed anyone to step in and rescue me. 

But, um... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... I have missed a couple of small calendar details when my mind is going that fast. Just minor things! And I've had to start double-checking tasks that usually just come automatically to me, just to be safe. I really don't want to let my boss down, so I try extra hard to catch any mistakes before they become an actual problem. 

Outside of work, though... I've actually pulled back a little from my photography outings, and, well, the mentoring I mentioned. I just... I haven't been feeling as present or as reliable as I should be, and I'd absolutely hate to disappoint the kids or be a burden to anyone. Do you think it's the right call to take a step back from those things for now? I just want to make sure I'm handling this the right way and not letting anyone down.
